data.description:
## Problem
`.rebar/enrich-drain.lock` is an `O_EXCL` existence lock with no owner stamp and no
staleness path: `enrich_drain._acquire_advisory_lock` creates it and
`_release_advisory_lock` unlinks it, so any drainer that dies between those two calls
leaks the file PERMANENTLY. Nothing ever reclaims it, and every subsequent drain
attempt sees `FileExistsError` and returns `None` — the caller then "skips silently".
Enrichment drains stop happening, with no error and no log line.

## Evidence
Found by the new `rebar doctor` lock-health report (ticket
metaphoric-fleeting-nutcracker) on its first run against this host's live tracker:

    enrich-drain: held 2266115s (~26 days); this lock carries no ownership stamp,
    so no holder can be named and staleness cannot be adjudicated

`ls -la .rebar/enrich-drain.lock` shows a 0-byte file, and no drain process exists. So
enrichment has been silently skipped on this checkout for roughly 26 days.

## Why doctor does not flag it
Deliberately. Doctor's staleness verdict is delegated wholly to
`lock_owner._mkdir_lock_is_stale`, which needs an ownership stamp. The drain lock has
none, so doctor reports the age and states `not-assessable` rather than forking a second
staleness heuristic. Fixing that honestly means giving this lock an owner, not teaching
doctor to guess.

## Direction
Give the drain lock the same shape the mkdir write lock already has: write the v2
ownership stamp (`lock_owner._owner_stamp()`) into the file at acquisition, and on
`FileExistsError` consult `lock_owner._mkdir_lock_is_stale`-equivalent adjudication
before deciding the lock is genuinely held. That reuses the existing decision table
(pid-recycle qualification, refuse-without-proof, wall-clock ceiling) instead of adding a
third locking dialect. Doctor's `not-assessable` row then becomes a real verdict for
free, since it already asks the shared function.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A drainer that dies without releasing does not wedge enrichment forever: a test
      leaves a stamped lock file naming a dead pid and asserts the next drain acquires it.
- [ ] A live holder is still honoured: a stamped lock file naming a live pid is not
      broken, asserted by a test.
- [ ] The stamp is the EXISTING v2 shape and the staleness adjudication is the existing
      shared function — no new staleness heuristic is introduced (verified by review of the
      diff: no independent age threshold, no independent pid probe deciding staleness).
- [ ] `rebar doctor` reports the drain leg with a real staleness verdict instead of
      `not-assessable`, and a dead-holder drain lock becomes a `stale-lock` finding.
- [ ] The silent-skip is no longer silent: a skipped drain logs at WARNING naming the
      holder, so a wedge is attributable without running doctor.
data.title: Leaked enrich-drain.lock wedges enrichment forever (no owner stamp, no staleness path)
